liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Little Bunny Foo-Foo** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer says the band playing this song is what makes the show seem historic to others; Reviewer singles out the Little Bunny Foo Foo moment as what the recording recalls [2][15][19]
- **Good Times Blues** (1 review): Reviewer says Brent puts his best foot forward on this and Never Trust a Woman [16]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Brent sings the first verse and a half, which the reviewer ended up enjoying [20]
- **Iko, Iko** (1 review): Reviewer found it pushed hard and fun, with Jerry's enunciation making a couple of funny lines audible [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **Audience**: rare: 12 archived performances [26]
- **Audience**: rare: 12 archived performances [26]
- **Little Bunny Foo-Foo**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **Audience**: rare: 12 archived performances [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-05-03.sbd-mtx.weber.gardner.1193.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 27 songs; 156 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1987-05-03.135937.dsbd.GEMS.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 150 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1987-05-03.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83738.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 150 min; rated 2.89/5 by 9 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls it one of the best-sounding Frost recordings available [22]
- **gd1987-05-03.166933.Frost.PaloAltoCA.Ultramatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t-flac1648**: soundboard; 21 songs; 154 min [4]
- **gd1987-05-03.166865.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 21 songs; 154 min [5]

## Around the show

- Beautiful weather for the afternoon show; a nearly full moon hung above the live oaks framing the stage [14]
- In the second set an owl swooped low across the mic stands, startling the band and crowd [14]
- First set is short, and Weir is barely present because he can't get his playing together [15]
- Weir is out of tune and struggles with his equipment throughout the show [17]
- Weir is out of tune and struggles with his equipment throughout the show [18]
- Reviewer was at the show in person and says the recording brought it back [19]
- Weir's mic keeps cutting in and out all show, which the reviewer finds distracting [20]
- Weir is out of tune and struggles with his equipment throughout the show [21]
- Reviewer calls it the weakest show of an otherwise great spring and summer [17]
- Reviewer calls it the weakest show of an otherwise great spring and summer [18]
- Reviewer calls it the weakest show of an otherwise great spring and summer [21]
- Many Frost tapes have an odd midrange problem; this one is better than most [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-05-03.sbd-mtx.weber.gardner.1193.sbeok.shnf**: taped by See info file; transferred by mixed by Sean Weber, converted to shn by Bill Gardner; source: DSBD/DAUD MIX [1]
- **gd1987-05-03.135937.dsbd.GEMS.flac16**: taped by PO and Stucco TINA Holmes; transferred by Jamie Waddell; source: Digital Soundboard > PCM copy > Sony L-750ESX-HFB Dynamicron EXCELLENT SUPER HIFI VIDEO CASSETTE-> Sony SLO-1800 STEREO VIDEOCASSETTE RECORDER-> Sony… [2]. Also: Recording supplied by PO and Stucco TINA Holmes; later tracked with Audacity and converted to FLAC level 8 [2]
- **gd1987-05-03.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83738.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Maxell MX90/Sony D5) [3]. Also: Pre-FM soundboard matrixed with a front-of-board Schoeps CMC3/MK2 recording; tapes from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [3]
- **gd1987-05-03.166933.Frost.PaloAltoCA.Ultramatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t-flac1648**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  January 31, 2024; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA) [4]. Also: This release is a 24-bit/96k to 16-bit/48k conversion of the 166865 ultramatrix [4]
- **gd1987-05-03.166865.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  January 31, 2024; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA) [5]
